Reasoning for the reversal: the tail-risk role p95-p99 was playing is already covered by RESEARCH_SPREAD_PARITY_MULTIPLIER_BY_ASSET (live_settings.py), a REAL-TIME guard that blocks new live entries if live spread actually runs materially above the research assumption -- padding the RESEARCH assumption itself with the same tail margin was double-charging every edge's cost model, and was confirmed to be silently excluding legitimate short-barrier/high-turnover candidates from ever reaching Gate C (e.g. DAX/trend_long's 5-bar lookback had gross_mean_R=+0.101, the BEST of its own grid, but was killed to net_mean_R=-0.072 purely by the old 3.83bps assumption on a ~22bps stop -- at the true 1.01bps median it would net strongly positive). This is a Gate B ranking change ONLY -- Gate A's gross screen stays cost-independent, and Gate C's real tick replay is unaffected since it never used an assumed cost_bps in the first place (see GATE_C rule below). RESEARCH_COST_BPS_BY_ASSET in live_settings.py was updated to these exact median values on 2026-09-24 -- same single number for Gate B ranking AND live enforcement, no separate 'tail' constant anywhere, so an edge tested/ranked at cost X is enforced live at cost X. Take the top 3 cells by this ranking as the Stage-2 finalist set, REGARDLESS of whether their individual net_R_per_mean_hold_bar values are positive or negative -- Stage-1 net is only ever a scout/shortlist tool from here on, never a pass/fail gate on its own.

GATE_C_stage2_authoritative_decision.when: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-25 for the finalist-COUNT part only ('typically 3 cells' -> now ALL Gate B positive cells, see GATE_C_ALL_POSITIVE_CANDIDATES_PLUS_PBO_2026-09-25 below). The rest of this entry (exact tick replay mechanics, executable_r>0 kill filter, argmax R/occupied_day winner selection) is UNCHANGED and still authoritative.
GATE_C_stage2_authoritative_decision.rule: exact historical bid/ask tick replay computes real executable_r (meanR), 95% bootstrap CI, PF, mean_hold_h, and R/occupied_day for every finalist. Filter to finalists with executable_r (meanR) STRICTLY > 0 -- if NONE of the finalists clear this bar, KILL the edge here regardless of how Gate A/B looked (this is the real, final kill gate now, not Stage-1 net_mean_R). If at least one finalist is positive, the WINNER is the one with the HIGHEST R/occupied_day among the positive finalists (R/occupied_day is the turnover-adjusted capital-efficiency metric -- it already rewards the 'shortest barrier settings that still clears cost' objective without a separate tie-break rule, since a fast, thin edge and a slow, fat edge with the same meanR will differ here). Use mean_hold_h as a secondary tie-breaker only when R/occupied_day is within noise between two finalists (prefer the shorter hold). AS OF 2026-09-25: this raw winner-selection must ALSO be checked against PBO/CSCV before being treated as final -- see below.
GATE_C_stage2_authoritative_decision.authority: executable_r is authoritative over net_mean_R whenever both exist for a cell, full stop -- Stage-1 approximates Stage-2, never the reverse. The 95%CI crossing zero is recorded but is NOT a hard gate (same caveat as every edge locked in so far) -- it's a promising-not-proven flag carried into Steps 01-09, which are the real confirmation.
GATE_C_stage2_authoritative_decision.output: the winning cell's (event_vol_lookback, event_vol_ewm_span, vertical_horizon, pt, sl) gets written into candidate_events.py/model_rows.py/edge.yaml, then export_research_dataset.py + Task2A rerun, then (on the VPS going forward) the full Step01-09 lifecycle, then promote_edge_status.py to deployability_pass only after a real Step09 PASS edge_manifest -- never set by hand.

GATE_C_ALL_POSITIVE_CANDIDATES_PLUS_PBO_.status: STANDING RULE as of 2026-09-25, discovered/decided during the DAX/trend_long calendar-time pilot (see calendar_time_labeling_REWRITE_2026-09-24 above). Read this before running Gate C on ANY edge going forward.
GATE_C_ALL_POSITIVE_CANDIDATES_PLUS_PBO_.why_the_old_top3_cap_was_wrong: the top-3 cap existed to keep Stage-2 'compute-affordable' -- but that assumption was never actually measured. Measured 2026-09-25 on DAX/trend_long: a 3-finalist+control Gate C run (4 configs, 8069 events) took 184.2s; a 10-finalist+control run (11 configs, SAME 8069 events) took 186.2s -- essentially IDENTICAL. Root cause: run_execution_finalist_mode's tick-replay loop iterates over the UNION of unique event timestamps across all tested configs, and because Gate C reuses the SAME persisted candidate_events.csv (the edge's currently-exported research_dataset) for every finalist regardless of that finalist's own event_vol_lookback/ewm_span (confirmed by reading _xef_artifacts/_xef_prepare -- each finalist's own Event_Vol is recomputed and looked up AT those fixed timestamps for barrier width/deadline, but the SIGNAL TIMES themselves never change), the total event count stays constant no matter how many finalists are added. Tick-file loading (the dominant cost) is therefore shared, not duplicated -- adding finalists only adds a cheap per-event PT/SL-touch check each. The ONLY part of Gate C that scales meaningfully with finalist count is the _xef_prepare preparation phase (computing each finalist's own full Event_Vol series over the whole bar history, ~278 EWM passes for 278 finalists) -- this is real but still modest (tens of seconds, not minutes, based on observed behavior) compared to the flat replay cost.
GATE_C_ALL_POSITIVE_CANDIDATES_PLUS_PBO_.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT_same_signal_stream: because every finalist is tested against the SAME persisted signal timestamps, Gate C does NOT validate whether a different event_vol_lookback/ewm_span would have triggered a genuinely different (more or fewer or differently-timed) set of CUSUM signals in the first place -- it only validates barrier-width/vertical-deadline execution quality given the CURRENTLY-LOCKED trigger stream. This is not a new limitation introduced by this rule change; it was already true when only 3 finalists were tested. It just matters more now that far more of the Event_Vol-lookback dimension is being explored at Gate C.
GATE_C_ALL_POSITIVE_CANDIDATES_PLUS_PBO_.new_rule: Gate C now tests EVERY Gate B cell with net_mean_R > 0 (not top 3) plus the current control geometry as a labeled comparison row. Confirmed on DAX/trend_long: 278 positive cells out of 405 total in the standard grid. Always pass --save so per-trade CSVs (v3_execution_trades_<label>_<stamp>.csv, with exec_r and event_ts columns) are persisted -- required for the PBO step below, and also just good practice (the earlier pilot Gate C runs on 2026-09-24 forgot --save and had to be partially re-derived from stdout logs only).
GATE_C_ALL_POSITIVE_CANDIDATES_PLUS_PBO_.pbo_cscv_check_MANDATORY_before_declarin: Testing hundreds of candidates and picking the best is EXACTLY the multiple-comparison overfitting risk AFML Ch.11 (SS11.6-11.8, p.157-167) exists to measure -- user explicitly required this, citing that DSR/PBO tooling was already built for this project. CONFIRMED 2026-09-25: it exists and is directly reusable. Use shared/backtest_statistics/afml_ch11_pbo_reference.py's cscv_pbo(performance_matrix, s=16, higher_is_better=True) -- a generic, pure-function AFML Ch.11 CSCV/PBO implementation already used elsewhere for structurally the identical problem (portfolio_allocator/08b_pbo_cscv_validation.py applies it to Step08's rolling-start scenario search, with the docstring itself noting 'that selection-among-many-candidates process is structurally the same multiple-comparison overfitting exposure'). Build the performance_matrix by loading each tested finalist's v3_execution_trades_<label>_<stamp>.csv, joining on the shared event_ts column (aligned across all finalists since they share the same signal stream, see caveat above -- a handful of rows may be missing per finalist due to differing coverage_rate, intersect to the common event_ts set), using exec_r as the per-observation performance measure, one column per finalist. Run cscv_pbo() and report PBO (fraction of train/test splits where the in-sample winner underperformed the out-of-sample median -- AFML says a result is trustworthy when PBO is low, and separately reports the book's own significance convention DSR>0.95 as a related but distinct check, see 07b_dsr_psr_validation.py for that) AND the performance-degradation slope (negative slope = higher in-sample performance predicts WORSE out-of-sample performance, the clearest overfitting tell) ALONGSIDE the raw argmax(R/occupied_day) winner -- never report the raw winner alone once more than a handful of candidates were tested.
GATE_C_ALL_POSITIVE_CANDIDATES_PLUS_PBO_.note_on_07b_vs_08b_tools: 07b_dsr_psr_validation.py (portfolio-level DSR/PSR, using MLAM ONC clustering for effective trial count) operates on the 21 CURRENTLY-DEPLOYED edges' own realized return streams -- a different level of analysis (across-edges) than what's needed here (across-geometry-candidates within one edge's own Gate C search). Use 08b's approach (cscv_pbo() directly) for Gate C candidate selection, not 07b.

gate_b_ranking_metric_FIX_bar_count_to_r.status: COMPLETE 2026-09-24. User raised a deep, correct methodological question: Quantara's bars (shared/bars/standard_quote_tick_builder.py) are causal daily tick-count-threshold bars (threshold_D = EWMA(prior completed daily tick counts) / target_bars_per_day, DEFAULT_TARGET_BARS_PER_DAY=50) -- genuine AFML Ch.2 information-driven bars, NOT fixed-calendar-time bars. A fixed bar count therefore spans a VARIABLE amount of real wall-clock time depending on intraday tick-arrival rate (fast during volatile/liquid periods, slow during quiet ones). net_R_per_mean_hold_bar (the original Gate B ranking metric) is a Quantara-specific construct, not something AFML/MLAM proposes -- AFML champions info-driven bars purely for sampling-quality reasons (closer-to-IID returns), never as a time surrogate. Using bar count to rank 'speed' could misrank two candidates whose tick-arrival-rate environments differ.

calendar_time_labeling_REWRITE_2026-09-2.status: COMMITTED 2026-09-24 -- this is being implemented, not just researched. User's own reasoning, verbatim-preserved: 'a 20 bar vertical barrier at 2:30PM for XAUUSD is not the same thing at 9:00PM for XAUUSD, so it is not consistent at all... we are using dukascopy, where its tick duration is different from this live broker's ticks.' Two independent, compounding reasons bar-count labeling is wrong: (1) time-of-day/session activity makes a fixed bar count span wildly different real durations (measured 2026-09-24 on DAX/trend_long: a nominal 20-bar lookback spans p10=3.3h to p90=16.0h in real time -- a 5x spread); (2) Dukascopy's tick density (used for ALL research/backtesting) differs from Moneta's (the live broker) tick density, so even a bar-count geometry that was internally self-consistent in research does not map to the same real-world holding time live. Calendar-time labeling is invariant to BOTH problems -- an hour is an hour regardless of session or broker tick density.
calendar_time_labeling_REWRITE_2026-09-2.q1_event_vol_empirical_test_RESULT: Tested 2026-09-24 on DAX/trend_long (real bar data, not simulated). Method: reproduced AFML Snippet 3.1 EXACTLY first (simple return, nearest-bar-at-or-before via searchsorted-then-minus-1, pandas default ewm adjust=True) as afml_literal_daily_vol, then a second variant using Quantara's own return/smoothing convention (log return, ewm adjust=False, from _hfg_event_vol) but with the lookback window changed from bar-count to the SAME calendar-time window, to isolate the window-unit variable from the return-type variable. Sanity check: corr(AFML-literal, Quantara-style-calendar) = 0.9998 -- confirms return-type barely matters, so the comparison below cleanly isolates window-unit. RESULT: corr(bar-count Event_Vol, calendar-time Event_Vol) = 0.93 (high but not 1.0); medians close (0.003874 vs 0.003809, ~2% apart) but PER-EVENT ratio distribution has p10=0.79, p90=1.29 -- roughly 20% of events would get an Event_Vol (and therefore PT/SL barrier width) 20-30%+ different under calendar-time vs bar-count. Real, non-cosmetic effect, worth fixing, being bundled with Q2 since both touch the same files and both require a full retrain regardless. Test script preserved for reference: was run from the session scratchpad, not committed to the repo -- re-derive from this description if needed rather than searching for the file.
calendar_time_labeling_REWRITE_2026-09-2.decision: Both Event_Vol lookback AND vertical barrier convert from bar-count to calendar-time, together, in one rewrite (not two separate cycles) since export_research_dataset.py + full Step01-09 retrain is required regardless of which one changed.

exact_mechanism_verified_against_AFML_pa.event_vol_calendar_time_lookback: BACKWARD-looking (a return window): use searchsorted(idx - Timedelta) THEN SUBTRACT 1 from the position -- the nearest existing bar AT OR BEFORE the target time (AFML Snippet 3.1's exact convention, p.44-45). Recommended concrete formula for Quantara: keep log return + ewm(adjust=False) (Quantara's existing convention, used everywhere else in the feature pipeline, and empirically near-identical to AFML's simple-return version per the corr=0.9998 test above) -- only the WINDOW becomes calendar-time via the searchsorted-minus-1 lookup, replacing the current close.shift(lookback_bars).
exact_mechanism_verified_against_AFML_pa.vertical_barrier_calendar_time_deadline: FORWARD-looking (an expiry deadline): use searchsorted(entry_time + Timedelta) with NO minus-1 -- the nearest existing bar AT OR AFTER the target time (AFML Snippet 3.4's exact convention, p.49: t1=close.index.searchsorted(tEvents+pd.Timedelta(days=numDays)), then filtered to t1<close.shape[0] to drop events too near the end of history). This is the OPPOSITE rounding direction from the Event_Vol lookback above -- backward-looking rounds to the past (conservative reference point), forward-looking rounds to the future (the position isn't 'expired' until real time has actually elapsed).

candlepiercing_long.thesis: Nison piercing pattern (Ch.4, p.55): gap-down open followed by a close penetrating >50% into the prior black body (but not fully engulfing it) at a recent local low -> long reversal. Genuinely different mechanism from candleengulfing_long (requires a GAP below the prior low, not just body containment) and candlehammer_long (two-bar confirmation, not single-bar wick). Who loses: shorts who added on the gap-down open (the most confirmed bears) are underwater as price recovers through >50% of the prior down-move within the same bar.
candlepiercing_long.design_note: Kept Nison's own 'more than halfway' (50%) penetration threshold as the mechanical definition rather than loosening it further, since it's already the core criterion distinguishing a piercing pattern from lesser on-neck/in-neck/thrusting patterns Nison explicitly says NOT to bother modeling separately -- exact penetration depth still carried as a feature (Piercing_Penetration_Frac) for the meta-model.

candleengulfing_long.thesis: Nison bullish engulfing (Ch.4, pp.42-48): two-bar body engulfment at a recent local low -> long reversal. Bar t-1 black body, bar t white body fully containing bar t-1's body. Who loses: shorts who entered during bar t-1's down move (and late shorts chasing that close) are underwater as bar t trades clean through their whole entry range, not just a single low tick -- a stronger short-squeeze setup than the single-bar hammer.
candleengulfing_long.design_note: Applied the recall-first lesson from candlehammer_long immediately: primary trigger only requires body containment + recent local low (5-bar), not a strict 'clearly definable trend' judgment call. Exact Nison engulfing-quality geometry (Engulfing_Body_Ratio, Engulfing_Prior_Body_Frac, Engulfing_Current_Body_Frac) carried as features for the meta-model to learn from.

candlehammer_long.thesis: Nison hammer (Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques Ch.4, pp.32-38): lower-shadow-dominant candle at a recent local low -> long reversal. Who loses: late short-side momentum chasers and stop-hunted longs wrong-footed by the intrabar rejection.
candlehammer_long.design_note: AFML Ch.3 requires the PRIMARY rule to be recall-oriented, not precision-oriented. First cut used Nison's exact textbook hammer geometry (lower shadow >= 2x body, upper shadow <= 0.5x body, 10-bar local low) and only produced 542 events over 70,442 bars (~0.77%) -- too precision-oriented/sparse for stable CPCV. LOOSENED to lower_shadow>=1.2x body, upper_shadow<=1.5x body, 5-bar local low, min_gap=3 -- exact Nison-quality geometry (Hammer_Body_Frac, Hammer_Lower_Shadow_To_Body, Hammer_Upper_Shadow_To_Body) still computed and carried as a FEATURE so the meta-model can learn to prefer near-textbook hammers. Rerun in progress to confirm new event count.

GATE_D_STEP04_CALIBRATION_MONOTONICITY_2.why_this_gate_exists: Gate A/B/C only establish that a geometry has real, cost-surviving raw signal. They say nothing about whether the meta-model, once trained, actually rank-orders opportunities by quality -- that is a separate, later failure mode (AFML's stated purpose of meta-labeling: the secondary model decides size/confidence, not direction). An edge can pass Gate C cleanly and still have a meta-model that does not discriminate.
GATE_D_STEP04_CALIBRATION_MONOTONICITY_2.rule: Read artifacts/thresholds/<edge_stem>_calibrated_threshold_sweep.csv after Step 04. Expectancy_r must rise as calibrated_probability threshold rises across the range with enough trades to trust each point (>= ~100-200 trades per threshold row as a practical floor; the file's own payoff_profile_valid flag and min_wins_required/min_losses_required=20 are the hard floor). A clean pass looks like absorption_long: 0.034 -> 0.044 -> 0.081 -> 0.094 -> 0.118 -> 0.295 (selected threshold, 215 trades, valid). A fail looks like trend_long (0.032 -> 0.027 -> 0.001 -> -0.163, i.e. monotonically WORSE with more confidence) or candleengulfing_long (declines 0.038->-0.001 across the trustworthy trade-count range, only 'recovers' on thresholds too thin to trust, 63 and 19 trades).

GATE_D_V3_AUC_ROC_2026-09-15.status: AUTHORITATIVE as of 2026-09-15, supersedes GATE_D_STEP04_CALIBRATION_MONOTONICITY_2026-09-14 entirely. Applies to every edge after Step 03 (generate_oof_predictions), before promote_edge_status.py may be run.
GATE_D_V3_AUC_ROC_2026-09-15.why_v1_and_v2_were_replaced: v1 (manual heuristic: eyeball calibrated-threshold-sweep, compare selected-threshold expectancy to first-tested expectancy) and v2 (Kendall tau trend test on that same sweep) both operated on shared/calibration Step04 output. User-driven review (2026-09-15) found three compounding, disqualifying problems: (1) the sigmoid calibrator (calibrated_p = sigmoid(intercept + coef*logit(raw_p))) is monotonic but nonlinear, so a fixed-step threshold grid in CALIBRATED space is an uneven, arbitrary partition of the real observations in RAW-probability space -- verified empirically that raw_probability on XAUUSD/rangestructure_long spans only [0.585, 0.890], meaning the sweep grid can crowd most trades into a few bins and strand others in sparse, unreliable tail bins independent of true model quality; (2) the per-edge selected_threshold this gated on is not even the live trading threshold -- that decision happens later, per-portfolio, at the allocator stage; (3) expectancy_r bundles execution/slippage/timeout noise the classifier was never trained to predict. Full-text search of both AFML and MLAM confirms the word "expectancy" appears in neither book, while AFML Ch.3 pp.52-53 explicitly names the ROC curve and precision/recall/F1 as the correct diagnostic for meta-labeling quality ("the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve of a binary classifier measures the cost of increasing the true positive rate...").
GATE_D_V3_AUC_ROC_2026-09-15.rule: Run shared/edges/gate_d_calibration_monotonicity.py --edge-root <edge_root> (add --write-report to persist the JSON under <edge_root>/reports/). It reads the per-row Step03 OOF predictions CSV (artifacts/oof/<asset>_<edge>_oof_predictions.csv -- NOT the Step04 calibrated threshold sweep) and computes AUC-ROC between raw_probability and quote_executable_meta_label across every OOF observation (no binning, no threshold grid, no calibration step involved at all). Tested via one-sided Mann-Whitney U against the null AUC=0.5, alpha=0.05. PASS requires AUC > 0.5 and p < 0.05. Because every OOF row is used (typically thousands), there is no multiple-comparisons problem requiring correction, unlike a threshold sweep. A non-gating diagnostic (Kendall tau, raw_probability vs quote_executable_r per row) is also reported for economic context but does not affect the verdict.
GATE_D_V3_AUC_ROC_2026-09-15.why_this_is_more_powerful_and_more_corre: Uses the classifier full OOF sample directly rather than ~10-20 binned points, so it has far more statistical power. Tests exactly the quantity AFML names for meta-labeling quality (ranking/discrimination via ROC), not a downstream, noisier economic proxy. Empirically re-run against every edge gated 2026-09-14/15 (JPN + XAUUSD): correctly flips XAUUSD trend_long, rangestructure_long and volatilitycarry_long to PASS -- these had the strongest Gate C exact-tick-replay evidence of their batches and were wrongly failed by v1/v2.

PORTFOLIO_ALLOCATOR_CALIBRATION_MISMATCH.bug: shared/calibration/fit_sigmoid_calibrator_and_thresholds.py produces TWO different, non-interchangeable values both named 'calibrated_probability': (1) cpcv_calibrate_edge() writes a CPCV-fold-AVERAGED value to *_calibrated_oof_predictions.csv -- a research diagnostic, since a given OOF row can fall into the test set of several different combinatorial fold-specific sigmoid fits and the stored value is the average of all of them; (2) fit_final_live_sigmoid() fits ONE sigmoid on all data and saves it to probability_calibrator_sigmoid_side_<side>.json -- this is the file shared/scoring/edge_scorer.py loads (confirmed by direct code trace, shared/edges/edge_layout.py line 442 asserts the filename) to score genuinely live/new signals, since CPCV cannot be run on data with no known outcome yet. portfolio_allocator/04b_build_threshold_grid_trade_ledger.py (PROBABILITY_COLUMN='calibrated_probability', line 48, enforced by a hard validation check at line ~701) and 04c_select_representative_threshold_candidates.py both built their entire threshold grid and selection logic on value (1) -- meaning the live trading threshold was being selected against a probability distribution live scoring would never actually produce.
PORTFOLIO_ALLOCATOR_CALIBRATION_MISMATCH.empirical_evidence: Measured directly on XAUUSD/rangestructure_long: recomputing 'calibrated_probability' from raw_probability via the saved single calibrator JSON does not reproduce the CPCV-averaged column (max abs diff 0.06). PORTFOLIO_ALLOCATOR_CALIBRATION_MISMATCH.why_fit_final_live_sigmoid_is_not_wasted: It is not unused -- it is the correct and only possible mechanism for scoring genuinely new live signals, since CPCV requires known outcomes to purge/embargo against and none exist for the future. The bug was never that fit_final_live_sigmoid was pointless; it was that the allocator's threshold-selection step should have reprojected the OOF sample through this same single live calibrator before building its grid, instead of reusing Step04's CPCV research diagnostic under the same column name.

GATE_C_RANKING_METRIC_LOCKED_compound_ve.why_the_old_metric_was_replaced: R/occupied_day = sum(exec_r)/sum(hold_days) implicitly assumes ZERO idle time between trades (costless instant redeployment) and is blind to real trade frequency (N). Verified empirically 2026-09-25: shortening the vertical horizon barely changed candidate_trades_per_week (e.g. DAX/trend_long: 37.8 -> 38.1/week despite hold dropping 16.9h->12.3h), meaning the metric's apparent 'turnover' improvement was mostly an artifact of dividing by a smaller occupied-time denominator, not genuinely more trading. GATE_C_RANKING_METRIC_LOCKED_compound_ve.why_slot_constrained_metrics_were_also_r: Tried slot=3 (matching live_manifest.json's max_open_trades_per_edge=3) -- REJECTED: that parameter is an OUTPUT of portfolio_allocator, a downstream stage that doesn't exist yet at Gate C and gets re-tuned against whatever clears the prop-firm challenge fastest; using it at Gate C is a look-ahead/circularity violation (user caught this). the_locked_metric.name: compound_velocity_score (allocator-consistent, allocator-agnostic)
the_locked_metric.source: Matches portfolio_allocator/04c_select_representative_threshold_candidates.py's own production 'Main 04C objective' (broker_growth_eval_for_f): score = velocity_calendar / max(mdd_abs_log, eps), where velocity_calendar = log_growth / edge_span_days and log_growth = sum(log(1 + f*exec_r)) over ALL resolved trades (no concurrency/slot assumption at all -- every trade counted, ordered by exit_ts, f=0.01 fixed nominal per-trade risk fraction, constant within an edge so it doesn't bias ranking toward any geometry).
properties: Calendar-time normalized (not occupied-time) -- doesn't reward hiding idle time.
LOG-compounding, not linear R-summing -- penalizes volatility/drawdown the way real capital growth actually behaves, matching AFML/Kelly-style objectives.
Drawdown-adjusted (Calmar-ratio-style) -- rewards smooth equity curves, not just total return.
No concurrency/slot assumption of any kind -- allocator-agnostic by construction, immune to the look-ahead problem the slot=3/slot=1 attempts both had in different ways.

GATE_C_RANKING_METRIC_LOCKED_compound_ve.why_shorter_did_not_win_everywhere_pt_sl: Checked two other possible 'shrink the barrier' levers before accepting the vertical-horizon story: (1) PT:SL ratio -- the search grid included 1:1, 1.5:1, 2:1; 18/21 final winners still use 2:1 (the WIDEST tested), confirming tighter horizontal barriers lose for the same reason shorter vertical loses (DAX/trend_long same H/E/Hv, PT:SL 1:1 vs 2:1: hold 13.4h vs 25.0h, but R/week 0.75 vs 2.50 -- clipping the target early captures a smaller, disproportionately less valuable slice of the same move). (2) EVENT_VOL_LOOKBACK_HOURS itself (the calendar-time H) -- checked whether shorter H mechanically shrinks the absolute barrier distance (Event_Vol) enough to matter: only 7/21 final winners have a shorter H than control, and only 9/21 have a smaller realized PT distance in bps -- H and realized Event_Vol magnitude do not move together simply (EWM span and the lookback interact, and log-return magnitude over a short window is not reliably smaller than over a long one). This lever is NOT what drives the improvements found; the vertical horizon (and occasionally EWM span) is doing almost all the work.

regardless of A/B. WINNER = argmax(compound_velocity_score), NOT argmax
(R/occupied_day) (retired: ignored idle time, could pick a "winner" worse
than control; slot-based alternatives also rejected — allocator look-
ahead / adverse selection). Formula mirrors portfolio_allocator/04c: ALL
resolved trades (no concurrency assumption), ordered by exit_ts, log_
growth = sum(log(1 + f*exec_r)) for fixed f=0.01, velocity = log_growth /
edge_span_days, score = velocity / max(max_drawdown_of_log_growth_curve,
eps). A positive estimate whose 95% CI crosses zero is evidence, not proof.

PRORATED compound-velocity series per candidate. PBO>=60% = reject as
noise (keep control); winner beats control AND PBO<40% = robust win;
otherwise keep control. Never report a raw argmax alone.

PBO_CSCV_METHODOLOGY_THREE_METRIC_JUDGME.trigger: User asked where the reject-if-PBO>=60% rule was sourced from. Grepped shared/backtest_statistics/afml_ch11_pbo_reference.py, portfolio_allocator/08b_pbo_cscv_validation.py, and all of shared/research: no hardcoded 60% (or any) reject threshold exists anywhere in the pipeline. The 60% number was stated by Claude during this session without a book citation, violating the AFML/MLAM sourcing discipline (always cite exact pages, never rely on memory).
PBO_CSCV_METHODOLOGY_THREE_METRIC_JUDGME.book_finding: AFML Chapter 11, pages 155-158 (CSCV/PBO). The book does NOT prescribe a universal PBO cutoff. It presents PBO alongside two other diagnostics as a joint read: (1) PBO itself -- fraction of train/test splits where the in-sample-best candidate underperforms the out-of-sample median; (2) the IS/OOS performance-degradation regression slope -- a steeply negative slope is a sharper overfitting signature than PBO alone; (3) Prob[OOS<=0] -- fraction of IS-winners that are net-negative out-of-sample, closest to the real-world risk of picking the backtest winner. The book's own worked example treats these three together narratively rather than gating on one number.
PBO_CSCV_METHODOLOGY_THREE_METRIC_JUDGME.decision: AUTHORIZED by user 2026-09-29: switch Gate C PBO/CSCV verdicts from a single 'PBO>=60% -> kill' cutoff to a three-metric written judgment (PBO + degradation slope + Prob[OOS<=0] read together) for ALL future edge-finding work, and to re-run this against the current live edges as a sanity check.

Default (no arg) preserves old raw-mean behavior, which remains correct for portfolio_allocator/08b_pbo_cscv_validation.py (whose real selection metric genuinely is net-profit mean).

v5.1 BROKER COST MODEL (authoritative; level/1.4x mode RETIRED -- audit only):
exact tick replay on the Dukascopy MID (validated: Dukascopy vs broker mid returns
60m corr 0.96-1.00) with the BROKER's spread, built from the broker's own MT5 ticks:
 - FIXED_POINTS when the broker's point spread is constant (p90/p10<=1.10), else a
   TABLE = mean spread by UTC hour-of-week x tercile of trailing-1-day realized vol
   (vol from the accurate mid path; Dukascopy's own spread is NOT used -- it is a
   fixed constant on USOIL/BTCUSD/NASDAQ/JPN/HK). Model type is chosen per asset per
   firm from the data.
 - LEVEL = broker's last 2 weeks (walk-forward: best 1-4 week forecaster on all 10
   assets), x live-entry calibration factor (actual/pred on real fills, shrunk by
   n/(n+30)). Converted to bps at today's ref_price and applied in bps to every era.
 - SWAP charged per rollover actually crossed by each trade (weekday server-midnights,
   Sat/Sun 0, triple day x3; validated on 409 real positions), at today's spec rate as
   a fraction of notional. COMMISSION = round-trip bps from the firm's deals/contract.
   SLIPPAGE beyond quote = measured ~0 on 213 Moneta fills (re-measure per firm).
 - NO spread guard in broker mode (modelled spread is the normal spread).
 - level_uncertainty_pct = the asset's measured 8-13 week forecast error (HK 3% ...
   USOIL 40%): ROBUSTNESS check, not padding -- see certification below.
5700 ms = measured live bar-close->fill median (v5; was 250). Extra cost stays 0.
Adds control automatically. ALWAYS pass --save — needed for PBO/winner.

v5.1 BROKER COST MODEL (authoritative; level/1.4x mode RETIRED -- audit only):
exact tick replay on the Dukascopy MID (validated: Dukascopy vs broker mid returns
60m corr 0.96-1.00) with the BROKER's spread, built from the broker's own MT5 ticks:
 - FIXED_POINTS when the broker's point spread is constant (p90/p10<=1.10), else a
   TABLE = mean spread by UTC hour-of-week x tercile of trailing-1-day realized vol
   (vol from the accurate mid path; Dukascopy's own spread is NOT used -- it is a
   fixed constant on USOIL/BTCUSD/NASDAQ/JPN/HK). Model type is chosen per asset per
   firm from the data.
 - LEVEL = broker's last 2 weeks (walk-forward: best 1-4 week forecaster on all 10
   assets), x live-entry calibration factor (actual/pred on real fills, shrunk by
   n/(n+30)). Converted to bps at today's ref_price and applied in bps to every era.
 - SWAP charged per rollover actually crossed by each trade (weekday server-midnights,
   Sat/Sun 0, triple day x3; validated on 409 real positions), at today's spec rate as
   a fraction of notional. COMMISSION = round-trip bps from the firm's deals/contract.
   SLIPPAGE beyond quote = measured ~0 on 213 Moneta fills (re-measure per firm).
 - NO spread guard in broker mode (modelled spread is the normal spread).
 - level_uncertainty_pct = the asset's measured 8-13 week forecast error (HK 3% ...
   USOIL 40%): ROBUSTNESS check, not padding -- see certification below.
5700 ms = measured live bar-close->fill median (v5; was 250). Extra cost stays 0.
Adds control automatically. ALWAYS pass --save — needed for PBO/winner.

WINNER RULE: filter to exec_mean_R STRICTLY > 0 — none clear it, KILL
regardless of A/B. WINNER = argmax(compound_velocity_score), NOT argmax
(R/occupied_day) (retired: ignored idle time, could pick a "winner" worse
than control; slot-based alternatives also rejected — allocator look-
ahead / adverse selection). Formula mirrors portfolio_allocator/04c: ALL
resolved trades (no concurrency assumption), ordered by exit_ts, log_
growth = sum(log(1 + f*exec_r)) for fixed f=0.01, velocity = log_growth /
edge_span_days, score = velocity / max(max_drawdown_of_log_growth_curve,
eps). A positive estimate whose 95% CI crosses zero is evidence, not proof.

statistics/afml_ch11_pbo_reference.py's cscv_pbo() (s=16) on a DAILY,

broker widening). Record break_even spread for the per-trade live guard. The old

QUANTARA V3 - NEW EDGE CREATION + FOUR-GATE GEOMETRY & META-MODEL RUNBOOK
v5.3, 2026-10-22 (after go-live 2026-10-19). Supersedes v5.2 (2026-10-17), v5.1, v5, v4.
Authoritative copies: Quantara_Runbook.docx Section 6A, and config/us500_edge_search_ledger.json -> RUNBOOK_v5.3_2026-10-22.
Running example: XAUUSD/compressionbreakoutcontinuation_short copied from BTCUSD/compressionbreakoutcontinuation_long.
RULE 0 - every command references the SAME edge_root you are building.

========================================================================
WHAT CHANGED IN v5.3 (2026-10-17 -> 10-22)
========================================================================
1. A constant-only edge change (e.g. EVENT_VOL_LOOKBACK_HOURS) changes the D1 candidate_logic_signature. The FAST
   provider (shared/edges/candidate_continuations/providers/*.py) must list the new signature in PROVIDER_SPEC
   supported_signatures, and D2/D3/D4 must be re-certified, or that edge runs AUTHORITATIVE (slower, still correct).
2. FAST-provider parity bug fixed 2026-10-18 in all 9 candidate providers: event-vol history was pruned at t-2L, but
   calendar_time_event_vol uses the latest bar before t-L at ANY age -> after weekend/session gaps > 2L, Event_Vol (and so
   TP/SL distance) was wrong (old 12-edge impact: docx Section 24.4). Provider tests must now include gaps > 2L.
3. Cost change at allocator time: after 00c/00d, compare each edge's 00d net R with its Gate C net R. If it falls by more
   than its stress margin, or to <= 0, re-run Gate C + PBO under the new model before deploying (BTCUSD timeregime:
   swap correction -> PBO 0.776 -> removed).
4. Repo path, interpreters and archive rule updated (below). edge_universe.json = 6 live edges (see STATE).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 0 - repo root and interpreters
------------------------------------------------------------------------
cd "C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Trading Models\trading_models_v2"
venv312 = edge research (Gate A/B/C lab, export, Task 2A, Steps 01-09, Gate D). venv39 lacks skfolio (Step 01 CPCV fails).
venv39  = portfolio_allocator, portfolio_live, Phase C/D scripts, live bot + dashboard. venv312's ast.dump() adds
          type_params=[] -> false structural-drift FAILs in Phase C/D; pandas 3 breaks allocator 04bb.
Research runs at BelowNormal priority; never touch, kill or reprioritize the live bot/dashboard processes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 - scaffold
------------------------------------------------------------------------
@'

------------------------------------------------------------------------

foreach ($f in "README.md","runtime.py","candidate_events.py","primary_side.py","edge.yaml","model_rows.py",

Copy-Item "$src\contracts\*" "$dst\contracts\" -Force

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 3 - identity replacement (Python, not Set-Content - avoids BOM)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
@'
from pathlib import Path
edge = Path("assets/XAUUSD/edges/compressionbreakoutcontinuation_short")
files = [edge / n for n in ("README.md","runtime.py","edge.yaml","candidate_events.py","primary_side.py",
  "model_rows.py","research_pipeline.py","export_research_dataset.py","feature_expansion.py","regime_features.py")]
files += list((edge/"contracts").glob("*")) + list((edge/"configs").glob("*")) + list((edge/"research").glob("*.py"))
rep = {"BTCUSD/compressionbreakoutcontinuation_long": "XAUUSD/compressionbreakoutcontinuation_short",
       "btcusd_compressionbreakoutcontinuation_long": "xauusd_compressionbreakoutcontinuation_short",
       "compressionbreakoutcontinuation_long": "compressionbreakoutcontinuation_short"}
for p in files:
    if not p.is_file(): continue
    t = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    for a, b in rep.items(): t = t.replace(a, b)
    with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as fh: fh.write(t)
    print("updated:", p)
'@ | python -
GOTCHA: edge.yaml's bare family: / candidate_event_generator: lines can be missed - grep and fix by hand.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
Short edge: side=-1, primary_side=-1, PT below entry, SL above:
  pt_price = entry_price * (1.0 - pt_multiplier * trgt)
  sl_price = entry_price * (1.0 + sl_multiplier * trgt)
Check candidate_events.py, primary_side.py, model_rows.py, runtime.py, export_research_dataset.py, edge.yaml.
Every feature goes through runtime.build_features(); no future information.
New thesis = new trigger written from scratch, recall-first (AFML Ch.3): wide net, false positives fine; carry exact
pattern geometry as a FEATURE, not a stricter gate. Porting a trigger to a new asset is not a new thesis.
Bar-level mechanisms only (Dukascopy research ticks vs broker live ticks differ) - no microstructure theses.
Every thesis must be tried on EVERY asset and BOTH sides; record it in config/cross_asset_thesis_coverage.json.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 7 - GATES A / B / C + PBO: GEOMETRY SELECTION
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Only Gate C locks a geometry. Calendar time (AFML Snippet 3.1 p.44-45, 3.4 p.49): Event_Vol lookback and vertical
barrier are real HOURS via shared/labels/calendar_time_barriers.py; EWM span stays bar-count.
Floor: >= 2000 model rows, strict, no exceptions.
COST for Gate A/B = mean_spread_bps_time_weighted (recent 2-week level) from
  portfolio_allocator/config/broker_profiles/<firm>_cost_models/<ASSET>.json (research firm = moneta).
  Not the Dukascopy median, not a 28-day tick median. No swap at Gate A/B.

--- GATE A: signal existence (405 cells, exactly this grid, never lab defaults) ---
python .\shared\research\v3_horizon_lab.py --edge-root <edge> `
  --event-vol-lookbacks 1,2,4,6,8 --event-vol-ewm-spans 20,50,100 `
  --vertical-horizons 1,2,4,8,16,24,48,96,168 --barriers 1:1,1.5:1,2:1 `
  --cost-bps <MODEL MEAN bps> --hybrid-fast-grid --save
KILL if best-cell gross_mean_R < +0.05 (no resurrection without a redesign).

--- GATE B: finalists (not a kill gate) ---
EVERY cell with net_mean_R > 0 goes to Gate C. Rank by net_R_per_mean_hold_HOUR. Use ONLY this run's fresh grid CSV.

--- GATE C: authoritative (venv312) ---
python .\shared\research\gate_c_runner.py --edge-root <edge> --grid-stamp <THIS Gate A stamp> `
  --cost-model portfolio_allocator\config\broker_profiles\moneta_cost_models\<ASSET>.json --out-jsonl <run.jsonl> --batch-size 120
= v3_horizon_lab --execution-finalists <ALL Gate-B cells> --execution-entry-delay-ms 5700 --execution-bootstrap-reps 2000
  --execution-spread-model broker --execution-cost-model <that json> --save, batched; logs each batch's run stamp.
Exact tick replay on the Dukascopy MID with the broker cost model: spread FIXED_POINTS or hour-of-week x vol TABLE at the
last-14-day level, swap per rollover crossed, commission (docx Section 23.2). 5700 ms = measured live bar-close->fill median. Extra cost = 0, no spread guard in broker mode. Control added automatically.
WINNER: among exec_mean_R STRICTLY > 0 (coverage >= 99%), argmax compound_velocity_score (log_growth = sum log(1 +
0.01*exec_r) over all resolved trades by exit time; velocity = log_growth / span_days; score = velocity / max
drawdown of the log-growth curve). None positive = KILL.
PBO/CSCV (AFML Ch.11 SS11.6-11.8): cscv_pbo(), s=16, from shared/backtest_statistics/afml_ch11_pbo_reference.py on a
DAILY prorated compound-velocity series per candidate, built from the Gate C --save output. PASS only if PBO < 0.5 AND
Prob[OOS<=0] < 0.5 (report the degradation slope). Else KILL. A borderline kill goes to Gate D only on an explicit user
decision (JPN volatilitycarry PBO 0.507 -> Gate D PASS, live). Driver (regression-tested):
  python .\shared\research\gate_c_pbo.py --jsonl <run.jsonl> <edge>
STRESS: re-run the winner at spread x (1 + level_uncertainty_pct); net R <= 0 there = flagged fragile. Record the
break-even spread for the live per-trade guard.

--- LOCK the winner in ALL FOUR places ---
 1. candidate_events.py: EVENT_VOL_LOOKBACK_HOURS, EVENT_VOL_EWM_SPAN
 2. model_rows.py: VERTICAL_HORIZON_HOURS, PT_MULTIPLIER, SL_MULTIPLIER
 3. edge.yaml labeling: block DIRECT children only: vertical_horizon_hours, pt_multiplier, sl_multiplier,
    reward_risk_ratio = PT/SL if present. Leave bar-count vertical_horizon and nested grid-cell notes untouched.
 4. export_research_dataset.py EXPECTED_* constants if present (a stale 702.306 rejected HK's correct lock).
Task 2A / Steps 01-09 read geometry from edge.yaml (trade_geometry.load_trade_geometry), not the .py constants -
grep that all four agree.

Two exact replays per event:
 - LABEL: triple barrier on the Dukascopy MID (zero spread, no carry, 0 ms) -> label_r / label_t1;
   quote_executable_meta_label = int(label_r > 0). Firm-neutral. Never label on Dukascopy bid/ask (D016).
 - ECONOMICS: research firm's broker cost model, 5700 ms -> executed_r = quote_executable_r. Keys research_firm and
   entry_delay_ms in portfolio_allocator/config/broker_repricing.json.
Check (EXACT): "Resolved quote-executable R mean" == Gate C winner exec_mean_R; coverage ~99.9-100%. A mismatch =
a lock place missed or the asi8 bug. Several edges: parallel per --edge-root, 5-6 concurrent max on 8 cores.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
01_feature_surgery_clustered_mda -> 02_train_meta_model_optuna -> 03_generate_oof_predictions ->
03b_oof_threshold_sweep -> 04_fit_sigmoid_calibrator_and_thresholds -> 04b_lock_selected_features_and_model_input_schema
-> 05_training_artifact_verifier -> 06_verify_runtime_scoring_ready -> 07_runtime_score_smoke_test ->

Driver: bash run_edge_lifecycle_01_09.sh (repo root) -> _lifecycle_logs/<ASSET>_<family_side>/{01..09}.log, timing.log,

Steps 01-03 train on the MID label; sample weights = class balance x AFML 4.6 return attribution x uniqueness.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 12B - GATE D: meta-model discrimination
------------------------------------------------------------------------
python .\shared\edges\gate_d_calibration_monotonicity.py --edge-root <edge> --write-report
AUC-ROC of raw_probability vs quote_executable_meta_label (= MID label) over every OOF row; one-sided Mann-Whitney U vs
AUC = 0.5. PASS = AUC > 0.5 and p < 0.05. Exit code IS the verdict - read the verdict: line. Never use
calibrated_probability, *_calibrated_threshold_sweep.csv or expectancy_r. Gate C passing does not imply Gate D, or the
reverse; a Gate D fail after a relabel is a real finding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 15 - hand-off to allocator + live (venv39; Quantara_Runbook.docx Sections 7-18)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every allocator run: 00a -> 00b -> 00c --firm <trading firm> -> 00d --firm <same> -> broker_repricing.json
enabled=true, firm=<trading firm> -> 01, 02, 03, 04b, 04bb, 04c, 04ca_analyze_rejected_edge_gates_optional, 04d, 05 ..
11 (STRESS_PASS) -> portfolio_live 00..04 -> Phase C/D if the edge set changed. Rerun only on a firm switch or an edge-
set change; no periodic 00c while live (the per-trade cost guard checks live spread at every entry).
Re-selection rule: every LIVE edge is re-run from Gate A whenever the cost model or label definition changes - old
geometries are invalid (10-17: HK drawdownhazard 702h -> 168h, XAUUSD volatilitycarry 168h -> 16h).
Any edge-source change, even one constant, invalidates D2/D3/D4 certificates for FAST routing (see v5.3 change 1).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
KEY RULES
------------------------------------------------------------------------
- A gross >= 0.05 -> B all net > 0 (fresh grid) -> C exec_mean_R > 0 + compound velocity -> PBO < 0.5 AND
  Prob < 0.5 -> stress -> 4-place lock -> export -> Task 2A (exact mean) -> 01-09 -> D (AUC, MWU p < 0.05) -> promote.
- Labels = Dukascopy MID. Economics = research-firm cost model at 5700 ms. Costs never enter labels.
- Calendar-time hours; EWM bar-count. 2000-row floor. Test long AND short on every asset.
- The allocator, not Step 04, owns the live threshold (per-edge selected_threshold is not live).
- Sizing = AFML 10.3 size x 10.2 budgeting per trade (risk / c_q concurrency quantile); no 10.4/10.5 (D017).
- Live code uses live_calibrated_probability, never the fold-averaged calibrated_probability (D015).
- Commit only approved edges, only when the user says so.
